title: Allah Has Bestowed Upon Us Everything
summary: Teach your child that every blessing around him is from Allah: food, water, toys, family, health. Whenever he enjoys something, remind him, "This is from our Lord." Teach him the phrase "Alhamdulillah" after eating and with every blessing. This builds a grateful heart that sees Allah’s hand in his life and plants the first meanings of ubudiyyah (servitude): that we love and thank the One who has bestowed upon us.
try_this: This week: Make "Alhamdulillah" a habit—after eating, upon seeing something beautiful. Count together three blessings every night.
reflection_prompts: How can you turn "Alhamdulillah" into an automatic habit for your child?
What blessings close to your child’s heart can you connect to Allah, the Bestower?

review_defects.why: Arabic 'اللعب' means 'play' (the activity), not 'toys' (the objects). The child enjoys playing, not necessarily toys. This is a slight shift in meaning.
